skill.name: applying-brand-guidelines
skill.description: Applies Acme-style corporate brand guidelines to document configurations and provides reference rules and validation checks for colors, fonts, layouts, tone, and messaging.
skill.summary: Apply consistent Acme-style branding to documents and validate content against brand rules.
skill.author: anthropics

content.value_statement: Teams often lose consistency when documents are created across formats and contributors. This skill applies brand colors, typography, layout rules, tone guidance, and validation helpers to keep outputs aligned.
actual_capabilities: Applies brand color, font, header, footer, table, and chart settings to document configuration dictionaries.
Provides standards for PowerPoint, Excel, PDF layouts, logo usage, tone, and data presentation.
Validates text for approved colors, fonts, brand name capitalization, prohibited words, and tone keywords.
Produces compliance scores with violations, warnings, and suggested fixes.
Includes reference guidance for accessibility, file names, department rules, and regional formats.
limitations: The included brand system is an Acme Corporation example and must be customized for real organizations.
The scripts return configuration objects and validation results, but they do not edit binary Office or PDF files directly.
Validation uses text pattern checks and cannot detect every visual layout issue.
The skill does not fetch updated brand rules, so users must provide current guidelines.

use_cases.title: Standardize Client Deliverables
use_cases.description: Apply consistent colors, fonts, slide structures, and tone before sending reports or presentations to clients.

use_cases.title: Check Marketing Drafts
use_cases.description: Validate draft copy and design references against approved colors, fonts, brand name usage, and prohibited terms.

use_cases.title: Prepare Operational Templates
use_cases.description: Generate reusable configuration guidance for spreadsheet, presentation, and PDF templates used across teams.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Branding
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the brand guidelines to this document plan. Focus on colors, fonts, logo placement, and tone.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Draft for Compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this draft against the brand guidelines. List violations, warnings, and practical fixes in priority order.

prompt_templates.title: Create Format-Specific Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for a presentation, spreadsheet, or PDF.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build brand guidance for a PowerPoint, Excel, or PDF deliverable. Include layout, chart, table, and footer rules.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Guidelines for a Team Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Customize these brand guidelines for a department workflow. Preserve required standards and note approved exceptions.

output_examples.input: A quarterly report draft uses red headers, mixed fonts, and informal wording.
output: Replace red headers with Acme Blue and use Acme Navy for body text.
Standardize all text to Segoe UI with the approved heading sizes.
Rewrite informal phrases into clear, professional, active language.

output_examples.input: A sales deck needs brand-aligned slide guidance before design work starts.
output: Use a title slide with a blue background, white title text, and top-left logo placement.
Use content slides with a blue title bar and white content area.
Limit each slide to six bullets and use approved chart colors only.

output_examples.input: A team wants to validate brand compliance for pasted marketing copy.
output: The review reports brand name capitalization, color, font, prohibited word, and tone issues.
The result includes a compliance score and targeted suggestions for correction.

best_practices: Replace the Acme example values with the actual brand palette, fonts, logo rules, and approved language.
Run validation on final copy and on design notes before producing the final document file.
Keep exceptions documented so special projects stay reviewable and consistent.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the sample Acme rules as production rules for another organization.
Do not rely on text validation alone for final visual approval.
Do not mix unapproved colors, decorative fonts, or competitor references into branded deliverables.

faq.question: What document types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for PowerPoint presentations, Excel spreadsheets, and PDF documents.

faq.question: Can it edit an Office or PDF file directly?
faq.answer: No. The scripts produce configuration guidance and validation results, not direct binary file edits.

faq.question: Can I use my own brand guidelines?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace the Acme example colors, fonts, tone words, and prohibited words with your standards.

faq.question: Does it check writing tone?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks prohibited phrases and looks for approved tone keywords in longer content.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed files use local rules and local validation logic.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for teams that create client documents, marketing drafts, internal reports, or reusable templates.
